title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant
NN5, Northampton
15.00 per hour
37.5 hours per week
Temporary to Permanent
ASAP
About the Role
Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity?
We are recruiting for an organised and proactive Accounts Assistant to join an established manufacturing business based in Northampton. This is a varied role offering the opportunity to support the day-to-day finance function.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous finance experience who enjoys working with numbers, takes pride in accuracy and is looking for a role with the potential to become permanent.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting the day-to-day running of the finance department and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Processing purchase invoices and ensuring transactions are correctly coded and recorded.
- Managing supplier accounts, allocating payments and investigating statement discrepancies.
- Completing bank, credit card and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Processing expenses and maintaining petty cash records.
- Assisting with supplier payment runs and monitoring outstanding customer balances.
- Supporting credit control and following up on overdue payments.
- Assisting with VAT records, VAT returns and other financial reporting requirements.
- Preparing journals, accruals and prepayments where required.
- Supporting month-end procedures, management accounts and year-end preparation.
- Maintaining financial schedules and assisting with payroll-related reconciliations.
- Liaising with external accountants, suppliers and colleagues to resolve financial queries.
- Ensuring financial records are accurate, organised and maintained in line with company procedures.

About You
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Bookkeeper or similar finance role.
- Good understanding of purchase ledger, reconciliations and general bookkeeping.
- Familiarity with VAT and month-end accounting processes.
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and accounting software, ideally Xero or similar.
- Able to manage competing priorities and work to deadlines.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a willingness to support the wider finance team.

Interested? If you have finance experience and are looking for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today to find out more, or please send your CV to (url removed)

Strong minute-taking or transcription experience

Competent IT skills

Emotional resilience when dealing with sensitive subject matter

title: Attendance Administrator
description:
Attendance Administrator

Location: Northampton, Northamptonshire
Salary (Apply online only) a day
Contract: Full Time, Temp to Perm
Hours: 8am to 4pm

Attendance Administrator

Are you organised, proactive and passionate about supporting young people to achieve their full potential? We are seeking a reliable and enthusiastic Attendance Administrator to join our busy secondary school office team.

The successful candidate will play a key role in monitoring and promoting student attendance, maintaining accurate records and working closely with students, parents/carers, teaching staff and the wider pastoral team to improve attendance and punctuality across the school.

Key Responsibilities
- Monitor and record daily student attendance, ensuring registers are completed accurately and promptly.
- Follow up on student absences, contacting parents/carers by telephone, email or text to establish reasons for absence.
- Maintain accurate attendance records and update the school's management information system.
- Ideally, use Arbor to record attendance, update student information and generate attendance reports.
- Identify patterns of absence and lateness, bringing concerns to the attention of the appropriate staff.
- Support the school in implementing attendance procedures and improving overall attendance rates.
- Assist with preparing attendance reports, letters and documentation for meetings.
- Work collaboratively with pastoral leaders, Heads of Year, the safeguarding team and the Senior Leadership Team.
- Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information in accordance with school policies and data protection requirements.
- Provide general administrative support to the school office when required.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who:
- Has excellent organisational skills and a strong attention to detail.
- Has good written and verbal communication skills.
- Is confident using IT systems, including Microsoft Word, Excel and email.
- Has basic knowledge of Arbor or experience using a school management information system (desirable).
- Can communicate professionally and sensitively with parents/carers and students.
- Is proactive in following up absences and resolving attendance queries.
- Can work independently, prioritise tasks and meet deadlines in a busy school environment.
- Understands the importance of confidentiality, safeguarding and accurate record-keeping.
- Has previous administrative experience, ideally within a school or educational setting (desirable).

What We Offer
- The opportunity to make a positive difference to students' education and wellbeing.
- A supportive and welcoming team environment.
- Opportunities to develop your administrative skills and knowledge of school attendance systems.
- Training and support to develop your understanding of Arbor and school attendance procedures, where required.

How to Apply

If you are an organised, approachable and motivated individual who would like to contribute to improving student attendance and achievement, we would love to hear from you.

title: Credit Control

Location: Northampton

title: Shipping Coordinator
description:
Shipping Coordinator

Location: Northamptonshire (Office Based)
Salary: 34,000

About the Role

We're recruiting on behalf of an established and highly respected manufacturing business that supplies products to customers across the UK and internationally.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Shipping Coordinator to join a busy, collaborative team where you'll play a vital role in ensuring the smooth movement of raw materials, finished goods and consumables. You'll be at the heart of the supply chain, coordinating shipments, managing logistics providers and ensuring customers receive exceptional service from order placement through to delivery.

What You'll Be Doing
- Coordinating inbound and outbound shipments of finished goods, raw materials and consumables.
- Preparing shipping, customs and Dangerous Goods documentation accurately and in line with customer requirements.
- Managing haulier and third-party logistics bookings while monitoring delivery progress.
- Liaising with Customer Service, Sales, Logistics, Purchasing and Production teams to resolve shipment and delivery issues.
- Reviewing and releasing raw material orders, checking stock availability, pricing and delivery schedules.
- Organising orders according to courier, destination, product type and shipping requirements.
- Producing pick sheets, shipping labels and shipment documentation packs.
- Coordinating import, export and third-party logistics activities.
- Maintaining accurate shipping records and supporting OTIF performance monitoring.
- Supporting complaint resolution, returns processing and general despatch activities when required.
- Ensuring compliance with customs regulations and Dangerous Goods legislation, including ADR, IATA and IMDG requirements.

Who We're Looking For
- Previous experience within shipping, logistics, export/import coordination or supply chain operations.
- Knowledge of Dangerous Goods shipping requirements would be highly advantageous.
- Strong IT skills, particularly within Microsoft Office packages.
- Experience of ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics AX would be beneficial.
- Excellent communication skills with the confidence to liaise with internal departments and external customers.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
- High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- A proactive, solution-focused approach and willingness to support colleagues across the wider team.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

What's On Offer
- Salary of 34,000.
- Monday-Friday working hours, 08:30am-5:00pm.
- Opportunity to join a well-established and growing organisation.
- Varied and challenging role within a busy supply chain environment.
- Supportive team culture with ongoing opportunities to develop your skills and knowledge.
- Exposure to international logistics, customs procedures and specialist shipping operations.

If you're an organised and detail-oriented logistics professional looking for a role where you can make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Impact Recruitment is working as an employment agency on behalf of our client.

All applications will be handled in accordance with current GDPR regulations.

Please apply with an up-to-date CV. Due to the volume of applications received, if you have not been contacted within 72 hours, your application has unfortunately been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Youth Employability Activity Coordinator - Northamptonshire
description:
Job Role: Youth Employability Activity Coordinator
Youth Engagement Employability Community Programmes Careers & Progression
Location: Northamptonshire/Leicestershire - Community-Based (Local Travel Required)
Salary: £32,000 per annum
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

Role Overview
Are you passionate about engaging young people, building confidence and creating opportunities that lead to meaningful careers?
We are recruiting an energetic and creative Youth Employability Activity Coordinator to design and deliver engaging programmes that help young people aged 18-24 develop the skills, confidence and motivation needed to progress into employment, education or training.
This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with experience in youth work, employability, education, careers guidance, community development, coaching, sports development, creative arts, training or support services who enjoys inspiring young people and helping them achieve their potential.
As a Youth Employability Activity Coordinator, you will create and deliver innovative workshops, projects and activities that develop employability skills, workplace awareness, resilience and confidence. Working closely with Mentors, employers and community partners, you will help participants take positive steps towards sustainable employment and long-term success.

Key Responsibilities
Activity Design & Delivery
- Design and deliver engaging, employment-focused activities for young people aged 18-24.
- Develop a rolling programme of workshops, projects and group activities aligned to participant goals and progression plans.
- Deliver sessions focused on:
- Employability skills
- Confidence building
- Teamwork
- Communication
- Digital skills
- Workplace readiness
- Personal development
- Utilise creative themes including:
- Sport
- Gaming
- Technology
- Virtual Reality
- Creative Arts
- Community Projects
- Volunteering Opportunities
- Adapt delivery to suit different learning styles, confidence levels and support needs.

Participant Engagement & Development
- Build positive, trusting relationships with young people.
- Use strengths-based and trauma-informed approaches to engagement.
- Support participants to identify their strengths, interests and aspirations.
- Help individuals develop:
- Communication skills
- Problem-solving abilities
- Resilience
- Professional behaviours
- Time management
- Confidence and self-belief
- Support learners to identify and articulate transferable skills for employment applications and interviews.

Careers & Employability Support
- Deliver practical employability activities and careers exploration sessions.
- Coordinate employer talks, careers events and workplace visits.
- Facilitate mock interviews and recruitment exercises.
- Support participants to understand different career pathways and labour market opportunities.
- Promote progression into employment, apprenticeships, education and training.

Partnership & Community Engagement
- Coordinate delivery with:
- Community Organisations
- Employers
- Education Providers
- Youth Services
- Local Authorities
- Specialist Support Providers
- Manage activity schedules, venues and logistics.
- Promote activities through face-to-face and digital engagement methods.
- Support outreach events and participant recruitment activity.
- Build strong relationships that enhance opportunities for participants.

Safeguarding, Inclusion & Wellbeing
- Promote a safe, inclusive and respectful learning environment.
- Support participants with diverse needs and backgrounds.
- Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns.
- Promote equality, diversity and inclusion in all aspects of delivery.
- Manage group dynamics positively and professionally.
- Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

Quality, Compliance & Performance
- Complete activity plans, risk assessments and evaluation reports.
- Maintain accurate records of attendance, participation and outcomes.
- Monitor engagement and progression against programme objectives.
- Collect participant feedback and use insights to improve delivery.
- Ensure compliance with safeguarding, GDPR, health & safety and quality standards.
- Support programme targets and positive participant outcomes.

Essential Criteria
- Experience planning, coordinating and delivering engaging activities for young people or young adults.
- Strong facilitation, presentation and group engagement skills.
- Ability to motivate and inspire individuals from diverse backgrounds.
- Experience supporting personal development, employability or progression outcomes.
- Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including:
- Low confidence
- Poor mental wellbeing
- Disability
- Neurodiversity
- Housing challenges
- Digital exclusion
- Limited work experience
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational and event coordination skills.
- Good IT skills including Microsoft Office and digital engagement tools.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and activities simultaneously.

Transferable Skills Welcome
We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds in:
- Youth Work
- Employability Services
- Careers Guidance
- Education & Training
- Sports Development
- Community Development
- Coaching & Mentoring
- Creative Arts
- Outdoor Education
- Social Care
- Housing Support
- Volunteering Programmes
- Customer Engagement
- Apprenticeships
- Mental Health & Wellbeing Services

If you have experience motivating people, running activities, building relationships and helping others achieve positive outcomes, we would love to hear from you.

Desirable Criteria
- Qualification in Youth Work, Teaching, Coaching, Careers Guidance, Employability or a related field.
- First Aid qualification.
- Experience delivering employability or personal development programmes.
- Experience coordinating events, projects or community initiatives.
- Knowledge of local labour markets, training pathways and apprenticeships.
- Understanding of safeguarding and working with vulnerable young people.

Additional Information
- Community-based role with regular travel across the local area.
- No homeworking due to the nature of the role.
- Enhanced DBS checks may be required.
- Flexibility to work across multiple venues and occasional non-standard hours where required.
- Ongoing training and professional development provided.

How to Apply
For more information or to apply for the Youth Employability Activity Coordinator role, please contact:
Robert Rowe

title: Receptionist
description: Receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record

title: Administrator
description: A great opportunity to be part of an excellent healthcare team where you will provide valuable administrative support and services to all members of the practice team. With your attention to detail, exceptional customer service skills, and experience of working within a fast paced environment, you will be the ideal addition to the practice family. Job responsibilities: Coding in a health care setting - eg: general practice Management of medical records Administrative support - processing of electronic documents Handling of incoming and outgoing emails, patient and hospital correspondence Customer Service/Effective Communication Experience of working as part of a team but also the ability to work independently when required. Experience of the various Microsoft packages: Word, Excel, Powerpoint. Experience of SystmOne would be advantageous although training will be provided to the successful candidate. Position is 37.5 hours per week over 5 days, between the hours of 8.30am - 5.30pm Retrieve and re-file records as requested, ensuring that strict alphabetical order is adhered to Ensure correspondence, reports, results etc. are filed in correct records Ensure records are kept neat and tidy and in good repair with all necessary information recorded correctly on the outer cover Summarising correspondence and medical records Patient deductions Administrative support Provide administrative support to members of the primary health care team in the following areas ensuring practice records are kept up to date where appropriate:- Cytology Pathology results Immunisation recalls Scanning of documentation Requests for copies of medical records from patients and solicitors Registering of new patients Read Coding information into patients medical records Medical reports for Insurance companies etc Incoming post including Royal Mail and hospital Electronic letters (EDIs) Provide cover and support to Secretarial Team Incoming and outgoing emails Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters.They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers.They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & Safety The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, the practice Health & Safety Manual, and the practice Infection Control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate
